answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by tying each agent identity to a costly, scarce bond that gets slashed when the agent signs conflicting claims. Splitting one operator into a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand bonds, a cost that grows fast. Like a jetty holding back the tide, the bond gives the network a physical barrier. Even a patient attacker with saffron-level budget has to wander far before the payoff arrives.
